seoTitle: Fix 'App Isn't Compatible' Error on Shopify
metaDescription: Troubleshoot the Shopify error blocking TikTok and other app installs, from checking eligibility and country restrictions to fixing install issues.
intro: The 'This app isn't compatible with your store' message shows up right when you're trying to move fast — connecting TikTok Shop, Facebook, or another sales channel — and Shopify doesn't explain what triggered it. Most of the time the cause isn't the app itself but a mismatch between the app's supported regions and your store's country setting. This guide walks through where that setting lives, how to confirm an app's requirements before you install, and what to check if a different app throws the same error later.

steps.heading: Understand why this error happens
steps.body: Shopify blocks an install when the app you're adding doesn't support your store's configuration — most commonly its country, but sometimes its plan tier or the sales channels it already has connected. TikTok Shop in particular is only available to merchants based in a set list of supported countries, so a store outside that list will see the compatibility message even though the app itself installs fine everywhere else. Facebook and other social-commerce apps enforce similar regional rules tied to where the platform can process payments and shipping.

steps.heading: Check your store's country in admin settings
steps.body: Your store's country lives under Settings → General, in the same section as your address, currency, and unit preferences. Because it's a long alphabetical list, it's easy to have picked the wrong entry when the store was first set up, or to have a business address in one country while genuinely operating in another — either one is enough to trip an app's eligibility check. Confirm this field matches where your business is actually registered before assuming the app itself is broken.

image.caption: The country selector under Settings, General — a long dropdown list where the wrong entry can silently block region-locked apps like TikTok Shop.

steps.heading: Review the app's own eligibility notes before installing
steps.body: Open the app's listing in the Shopify App Store and read the pricing and requirements section near the Install button — this is where TikTok, Facebook, and similar apps note if they're limited to businesses based in specific countries. If your store's country isn't on that list, no amount of retrying the install will fix it; the app is genuinely not available to you yet, and you'd need a different integration or a business entity registered in a supported region.

image.caption: The TikTok app listing in the Shopify App Store, showing pricing and the Install button — check the requirements text above this before installing.

steps.heading: Complete onboarding once the install succeeds
steps.body: If your store does meet the eligibility requirements, installing the app drops you into its own onboarding panel inside Shopify admin rather than finishing everything automatically. For TikTok, this means working through a task list — setting up TikTok Business and TikTok Ads Manager accounts, authorizing data sharing, and building out your presence — before ads or shop features actually go live. Skipping tasks in this checklist is a separate, common reason people think the app is 'still not working' when really it's just unfinished setup, not a compatibility error at all.

image.caption: The TikTok app's onboarding panel inside Shopify admin, showing an 8-step task list to connect accounts and authorize data sharing.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot other apps with the same error
steps.body: For non-TikTok apps showing this same message, work through the same two checks: confirm your store's country under Settings → General, then read the app's own requirements on its App Store listing page. If both look fine and the error persists, try removing and reinstalling the app, clear your browser cache, or attempt the install from a different browser, since a stuck session can occasionally cause a false compatibility message. If it still fails after that, the app's own support team — reachable from its App Store listing — can confirm whether your store type is genuinely unsupported.

steps.heading: Avoid the error on future installs
steps.body: Before installing any new sales-channel app, get in the habit of checking its requirements section first rather than clicking Install and troubleshooting after the fact. It takes a few seconds and saves you from chasing a phantom bug when the real issue is simply that the app doesn't operate in your store's country yet. Keeping your store's country setting accurate from day one also prevents a whole category of these errors before they start.

faq.question: Why does Shopify say an app isn't compatible with my store?
faq.answer: This typically relates to store eligibility, country restrictions, or configuration mismatches between your store and the app's requirements — check the app's listing page for its supported regions.

faq.question: Is this error specific to TikTok?
faq.answer: No, while TikTok is a common example, the same compatibility error can appear when installing Facebook or other third-party sales-channel apps that enforce regional availability.

faq.question: Can country restrictions cause this error?
faq.answer: Yes, some apps are only available in certain countries, and your store's country is set under Settings → General — installing from an unsupported region will trigger this compatibility error regardless of your plan.

faq.question: What should I check first when I see this error?
faq.answer: Start by checking your store's country under Settings → General, then compare it against the requirements listed on the app's own Shopify App Store page.

faq.question: The app installed but features aren't working — is that the same error?
faq.answer: Usually not. A successful install with missing features almost always means an onboarding task, like account authorization, hasn't been completed yet rather than a compatibility block.
